newsitem.title: FRANCE: Portugal president urges EU, NATO expansion dates.
newsitem.headline: Portugal president urges EU, NATO expansion dates.

text.p: Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio on Monday urged that a timetable be drawn up for a gradual integration of Europe's former Communist nations into the European Union and NATO.

"The gradual integration of central and east European states in all European and western institutions is vital," he said in a speech to the parliamentary assembly of the 39-nation Council of Europe in Strasbourg.

The Socialist president, addressing the Council which seeks to promote democracy and human rights in Europe, said it was "hardly reasonable to put off any longer the setting of calendars and timetables for enlargement".
Enlargement was "decisive both to consolidate democratic governments and to guarantee stability and security in a vast European region", he said.

Sampaio said Russia, which has opposed the eastwards expansion of NATO, should not be excluded. "We must try to ensure recognition of its interests within a European framework of stability and security," he said.
